answer: Randomness-chained registration. Each identity must submit a fresh random seed drawn after a public beacon fires; the seed maps it to one cell in a meadow of shards, and only that shard may forge its credential. Seeds are validated post-hoc, so an attacker cannot precompute placements or batch-register ahead of the beacon. Each attempt costs one independent beacon window and a full orchard of decoy identities that mostly land in already-crowded shards and get rejected.
